claude_only.name: Which authoritative scheme identifier designates this monetary unit, and what is the code value within that scheme?
When no governed external identifier exists, what surrogate key is assigned and how is its collision resistance and reuse policy defined?
How is a reused or historically ambiguous code disambiguated between distinct units that carried the same alphabetic code at different times?
Does this identifier denote money, or a fund, precious metal or testing placeholder that must never be treated as spendable money?
Which unit kind does this record assert - national currency, supranational currency, fund unit, precious-metal unit, special drawing right, special-purpose code or digital token unit?
For a digital token unit, does it reference a single official currency, a basket or other value, or nothing at all, and which regulatory subclass follows?
What semantics apply when a special-purpose code is present, and which operations must be blocked?
Where two authorities classify the same unit differently, which classification governs for a given consumer?
What minor unit value does the governing scheme publish for this unit, and is it defined at all?
From which effective instant does the current minor unit apply, and what value applied before it?
When a target payload permits more or fewer fractional digits than the minor unit, which constraint governs and how is the divergence recorded?
What is the named subdivision of the unit and does any non-decimal or legacy subdivision remain in force?
What is the official name of the unit and which authority is the source of that name?
Which local, plural or transliterated names and scripts are in authorised use for this unit?
Which symbol is associated with the unit, and how is it disambiguated where the same symbol serves several units?
How does the record keep locale presentation separate from the stored value so that formatting never becomes the source of truth?
Which instrument form does this class assert, and against which taxonomy is that form defined?
Which monetary unit denominates this instrument, and can a single instrument class be denominated in more than one unit?
On what medium, ledger or infrastructure does the instrument's existence depend, and what happens to the instrument if that medium ceases?
What test distinguishes this instrument from a non-monetary claim such as a loan, voucher, loyalty balance or security token?
Is the instrument transferable in bearer form, or does transfer require registration, issuer involvement or operator participation?
Are units of this instrument class fully fungible with each other, and what conditions break fungibility?
What is the smallest transferable quantity of the instrument, and is it the same as the unit's minor unit?
Can value in this instrument be transferred without connectivity to the issuer or ledger, and under what limits?
Which governed entity identifier designates the issuer, and which register was used to verify it?
On what legal basis does this entity have authority to issue the instrument, and in which jurisdictions does that basis hold?
Where issuance, distribution, custody and ledger operation are performed by different entities, which entity holds which role?
If the instrument has no identifiable issuer, how is the absence recorded and what downstream constraints follow?
Against whom does the holder hold a legal claim, and is that claim against the issuer, the reserve assets, or neither?
On what terms can the instrument be redeemed - at what value, within what period, subject to what fees or minimum amounts?
What assets back the instrument, how are they segregated and safeguarded, and how frequently is their composition disclosed?
What stabilisation mechanism maintains value, and what is the documented behaviour when it fails or redemption is suspended?
Is this instrument central bank money, commercial bank money, or a settlement asset that is neither?
What credit and liquidity risk does a holder or receiver bear when accepting this instrument in settlement?
To which categories of party is this settlement asset available, and is availability restricted to eligible institutions?
If this settlement asset becomes unavailable, what substitute is designated and on what authority?
Does delivery of this instrument discharge a monetary obligation in a given jurisdiction, and on what legal basis?
Does finality for this instrument arise from the instrument itself or only from the rules and legal basis of a transfer arrangement?
After delivery of the instrument, under what circumstances can the transfer of value still be unwound?
On what grounds may a creditor lawfully refuse this instrument despite its status?
In which jurisdictions does this instrument hold legal tender status, and which legal instrument confers it?
What quantitative limits bound the obligation to accept, such as caps on coin counts or cash payment thresholds?
When did the current legal tender status take effect, and what status preceded it?
For instruments without legal tender status, what governs acceptance and how is that recorded distinctly from tender status?
Which jurisdictions and territories use this unit as money, and on what basis does each do so?
Which authority exercises monetary sovereignty over the unit, and is that authority distinct from the users of the unit?
Does another monetary unit circulate in parallel in any of these territories, and how are the two related?
What accession, substitution or secession events changed the territorial footprint, and when did each take legal effect?
Under which authorisation regime and register entry is the issuer permitted to issue this instrument?
What is the current authorisation state, and when was that state last verified against the register?
Across which additional jurisdictions does the authorisation extend by passporting or recognition, and under what conditions?
How is an instrument recorded when its issuer is unauthorised, unregulated or outside any authorisation regime?
What limits apply to how much of this instrument a party may hold, and to which party categories do they apply?
Is conversion of this unit into other units restricted, and by what mechanism - controls, licensing, quotas or suspension?
Which restrictive-measure or sanctions regimes affect the unit, instrument or issuer, and where is the authoritative list held?
When restrictions from different authorities conflict, which prevails for a given party and transaction context?
What lifecycle state does this unit occupy, and which registry list is it currently carried on?
Which numbered amendment introduced or retired this unit, and when was it issued versus when did it take effect?
When did the local record first observe this state, and what lag existed between the effective instant and the observation instant?
How is a unit handled between its announcement and its effective date, when both the old and new unit are valid for different purposes?
Which unit succeeds this one, and what is the fixed conversion factor and its direction of expression?
What rule preserves continuity of instruments and obligations expressed in the retired unit?
Must historical records be restated into the successor unit, or preserved in the original unit with the mapping applied at read time?
During a changeover period, how are amounts, prices and obligations disambiguated between the retiring and successor units?
Which series exist for this instrument class and what denomination set does each carry?
Is each series still being issued, and if issuance ceased, when and by whose decision?
For a ledger-based instrument, which contract or protocol version and ledger identify the current series, and what fork or migration history precedes it?
What series-specific authentication or validation features must a verifier check, and where is the specification published?
Has issuance ceased, has legal tender status ended, or both - and on what dates did each occur separately?
Until when, where and by whom can the instrument still be exchanged for current money, and is the guarantee open-ended?
For a terminated electronic money or token programme, what redemption obligation survives and how is it funded?
What becomes of value never presented for exchange, and who acquires the benefit?
How is the numeric value bound to its unit reference so that the pair cannot be separated in transit or storage?
What scale is permitted for this amount, given the unit's minor unit and the narrower limits of the target payload type?
What numeric representation preserves exactness, and what representations are prohibited?
What do a negative amount and a zero amount mean in this model, and where must direction be carried instead?
Which rounding mode applies to a converted or computed amount, and what is its normative source?
How is the full published precision of a rate preserved through the computation, and what intermediate rounding is prohibited?
When a total is allocated across parts, what rule assigns the remainder so that the parts sum exactly to the total?
How is a divergence between this model's rounding result and a counterparty's result detected, evidenced and resolved?
Which ordered pair does the rate express and in which direction is the quotation stated?
Is this a legally fixed conversion factor, a published reference rate, a scheme rate or a transacted rate?
At what instant was the rate determined and at what instant published, and in which time zone was each stated?
What does the publisher say the rate may and may not be used for, and what fallback applies when it is unavailable?
For each governed field, which external body is the master and what is the locator of the source of record?
How does the local record learn of amendments at each master, and what is the maximum acceptable staleness?
Who is accountable for the correctness of this local record, and what decisions may they take without the master's involvement?
Which fields are copied from a master and which are locally asserted judgements, and how is the difference made visible to consumers?
Which external scheme identifiers map to this unit or instrument, and what is the equivalence strength of each mapping?
What evidence supports any claim of conformance to an external standard, and where is only alignment claimed?
Where two schemes disagree about this unit or instrument, how is the conflict recorded and surfaced to consumers?
How is drift handled when one scheme publishes a change that another has not yet reflected?
For each target projection, what binding rules govern how a unit reference and an amount are rendered and parsed?
Which externalised code sets does a projection depend on, and how is their republication cadence tracked?
What information defined in this model cannot be carried by a given projection, and how is that loss disclosed?
How does a projection behave when it encounters a unit code that its bound code set does not contain?
Which validation rules apply to this record, and which are blocking versus advisory?
What evidence is retained for each validation run, and how are effective time and observation time recorded separately?
What happens to a record that fails a blocking rule - is it quarantined, superseded, or published with a defect marker?
How is a record detected as stale relative to its master, and what confidence signal is exposed to consumers?
Which parts of the record may be published openly and under what licence or reuse terms from the upstream source?
Which attributes are restricted, on what basis, and to which roles are they visible?
How long are superseded unit states, succession mappings and rate snapshots retained, and what justifies indefinite retention?
Under what circumstances may data be deleted, and what must survive deletion to preserve the audit chain?
What access events are logged, and how long is the access log itself retained?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master identifier of this monetary unit, and is it an ISO 4217 alphabetic code, numeric code, or an issuer-assigned identifier for an unlisted unit?
Which geopolitical entity or monetary union is listed as responsible for this unit, and does that entity share the unit with others?
Which Maintenance Agency list version and amendment first carried, changed or withdrew this code?
What is the decimal relationship between this unit and its minor unit, and is that minor unit used in banking records of value?
Is the listed code a state currency, a fund, a precious metal, a special/test code, or the SDR?
May amounts in this unit be recorded with a fractional scale other than the ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent, and who authorises that exception?
Is this unit the SDR (XDR), another currency basket, or an ordinary national unit?
Which listed currencies and fixed amounts compose the SDR or other basket, and who may change that composition?
Which classes of holder are legally eligible to hold this reserve instrument, and are private parties excluded?
Has this unit been redenominated, replaced or moved to the historic list, and what is its successor or predecessor code?
What official conversion factor applies, and what are the dual-circulation and dual-price-display intervals using event time distinct from catalogue ingestion time?
Which successor unit, predecessor unit and issuing entity records must remain linked so historic amounts can be restated?
Which monetary instrument class is this, and which SNA/MFSM category does it align to?
In which listed monetary unit is this instrument class denominated, and is foreign-currency denomination permitted?
Is this object money, a payment instrument that is not money, or both, and which sibling model owns the payment act?
Does this instrument meet the electronic-money tests of stored value, claim on issuer, issuance against funds, and acceptance by a third person?
On what terms is outstanding electronic money issued and redeemed, and is interest prohibited?
Is circulation closed or open, and which limited-network or closed-loop uses are excluded from this instrument class?
Is this instrument class convertible at par into public money and directly usable for third-party payments without penalty?
Does a good-faith transferee take free of prior claims, and is transfer by possession or by account assignment?
Under what impairment, restriction or overdraft conditions does this class lose transferable-deposit or currency treatment?
Which monetary authority or authorised issuer may create this instrument class, and under what legal mandate?
On whose balance sheet is outstanding stock a liability, and do holders bear issuer credit risk?
Which organization, state or currency-union records are referenced as issuer or monetary authority without inlining those entities?
What issuance, allocation, load, redemption or cancellation event changed circulating stock of this instrument class?
When did the stock event occur in the world, and when was that event observed or ingested?
What quantity remains outstanding as issuer liability after the event, in which unit, excluding holder-level accounts?
Which series and face denominations are currently legal tender, redeemable only, or demonetized?
What issuing-authority notice is the evidence for series validity or demonetization, and what is its observation time?
Is this piece excluded from financial currency because it is commemorative, intrinsic-value or not in active circulation?
Is this object money, currency, legal tender, or a combination, according to the applicable monetary law rather than ISO listing alone?
Which monetary-law instrument grants official-unit or legal-tender status, and which monetary authority administers it?
In which jurisdictions or currency-union territories does this legal-tender or official-unit status apply, including dollarized or union members?
What legal-tender, coin, cash-payment or AML thresholds constrain use of this instrument class in a given territory?
Is outstanding holding of this instrument class capped, and is the cap a property of the instrument rather than of an account product?
Must a creditor accept this instrument, and are there exceptions for technology barriers, large amounts or private-contract opt-out?
Is this instrument retail CBDC, wholesale CBDC, tokenised commercial-bank money, or e-money, and is it a direct central-bank liability?
Does this CBDC create a new instrument class or reuse cash, deposit or e-money legal rules, and which sibling owns wallets and payments?
Which holding caps, programmability, interest, identity and offline rules attach to the instrument class itself?
Is this object digital fiat (in-scope instrument class), an e-money token referencing one official currency, or a FATF virtual asset outside this model?
If a DTI or unofficial ticker exists, does it identify a token rather than an ISO 4217 unit, and must both identifiers be stored without conflation?
What primary legal instrument, if any, grants this unofficial asset legal-tender status, and does that conflict with ISO 4217 non-listing and IMF currency tests?
Which 2008 SNA financial-instrument class applies to this unit or instrument class, and is electronic money treated as a deposit rather than as currency?
Is this instrument type included in the compiling jurisdiction's broad money, and does inclusion depend on holder sector rather than on a single holder's balance?
Where MFSMCG and SNA wording differ from ISO 4217's definition of currency, which scheme is being used for this record and what conflict is flagged?
Which identifier is master for this unit, and which ISO 20022, DTI or unofficial identifiers are aliases rather than masters?
Which ISO 4217 MA list version and ISO 20022 code-set version is this record pinned to?
If a payment message carries ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode, does it resolve to this unit without implying that this model implements ISO 20022 payments?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
